Messages.Author: Xian
Messages.Body:
"Jeffrey Moore" <Trut...@webtv.net> wrote in message
news:10424-3A...@storefull-145.iap.bryant.webtv.net...

> Rules wise, what do you have against a vamp being toasted by

> stealing? When playing this weekend, one player brought out Tremere and

There is no logical reason that a vampire should burn when blood that it does
not have is stolen. As Joe pointed out, a punch for 1 should do the same
thing then. If you want to bring RPG/WoD perspective, it's pretty much the
same. The Tremere *can* use Theft of Vitae on a vampire without blood, but it
doesn't do anything. It's pretty simple.

> the gang was laughing like Dr Evil and crew when they were going get one
> hundred billion dollars. The Tremere are a JOKE in this game. From

The Tremere are a joke because people insist on playing them wrong.
Thaumaturgy on its own is not sufficient to stand up to a top-class combat
discipline...such a Potence. Thaumaturgy needs support from other cards.
Telepathic Tracking is a great help. So is Thoughts Betrayed. Using
maneuvers or damage prevention from either skill-less cards, equipment,
Celerity, or Fortitude works well.

Yes, Thaumaturgy has some really nasty strikes. However, they can't be used
without the proper support. Much like a weenie Potence IG deck won't work if
you can't maneuver to close range, or a Brujah pitch deck doesn't work nearly
as well at close range, Thaumaturgy needs some form of combat support to
prevent S:CE as well as damage to your own minions. As long as people keep
trying to run Thaumaturgy as a premiere combat discipline without adequate
support from other sources, they will continue to fail.

> reading the novels and books even the Sabbat cringe at the word Tremere.

That's not because the Tremere wade into combat and kick ass like the Brujah
or the Gangrel. It's because the Tremere are fucking sneaky and cruel as
hell. So play that way, dammit. Don't get stuck in a straightforward mode
where you're trying to beat other combat decks at their own game.

Here are some suggestions:

If your playgroup sees lots of blocking, try experimenting with a dom/for/tha
deck like my "I Used to Think that the Day Would Never Come, that My Life
Would Depend on the Morning Sun"[1]...which I am in the process of revising,
because my playgroup *finally* caught on. I played it in a tournament
recently, and with a little more luck, would have walked away with more than 1
VP. An ill-timed vote when I didn't have Kindred Coercion in my hand kept me
from sweeping a table, and a cross-table Conditioning added *after* the
Deflection to me proved my downfall in separate rounds. Well, that, and my
sleep-deprived play may have proved a factor...Mark ShaneWood might be the
best judge there. However, the previous time I played it, I swept a 5 player
table that included a stealth-bleed deck, a vote deck, and two brutal combat
decks.

If your playgroup sees lots of low-stealth actions or Bruise & Bleed decks,
try playing an intercept deck like the one I just posted in the VEKN Tremere
Clan Newsletter for November. Intercept the crucial actions, or ones where
the minions are weak.

If your playgroup is focused on combat, try something different...perhaps a
Tremere dom/aus deck that focuses on bleeding and uses bounce and Obedience
for defense.

If you're bored and interested in something challenging, play a Cryptic
Mission deck as outlined here:
http://www.waste.org/~xian/geek/jyhad/news/tremere1-6.html

> I feel this "metaphor" of the WOD should be somewhat accurate. I am
> not alone in this thought. LET'EM FRY!

No, you're not alone. There are a number of other misguided sods out there
that agree with you. People that believe that Blood to Water should burn
vampires as well. Stealing/burning blood was never supposed to burn
vampires...there's no reason to make it do so now. The Tremere *are*
strong...the problem is that people play them wrong...they are not meant to
stand toe to toe with the Brujah or the Gangrel. They're a little bit more
intelligent than that. So freakin' play them that way, already.

Xian
Chronicler of Clan Tremere

Messages.Author: Tim Fletcher
Messages.Body:
I hate to whinge like, well, a whinger, but the Tremere get a raw deal in
V:TES anyway.
Thaumaturgy (as I have have to explain to countless GMs over the years) is
not a combat
discipline. Its primary use is political, to either set Vampires up to be
rescued (thus owing
a boon) or to get them out of scrapes they were already in (likewise). This
is not
represented in any way in the card game. There are two non-combat cards, and
although
Cryptic Mission in theory represents the non-combat side (and therefore of
course shouldn't
burn vampires because no amount of discrediting will actually kill you),
it's rather restricted
compared to the newly expanded Dementation which now features more ways to
send you
mad than many other disciplines' action cards put together.

So the reason people play Tremere as a combat deck is because that's how
they're presented.
If you just want access to Auspex and Dominate, play Malk or !Ventrue.

The Sabbat do not hate and revile the Tremere because of their other
disiciplines...

Messages.Author: Halcyan 2
Messages.Body:


I always thought that THE most important aspect of Thaumaturgy (and the
Tremere) was flexibility.

Sure, the Tremere (in the RPG) are rightly feared in combat. In the past, when
the Sabbat were planning an attack, they'd only be calculating in the Brujah,
Gangrel, and Tremere presence in the city. Although VTES "tries" to make
Tremere decent in combat, it hasn't really been very successful.

But still, flexibility is the greatest power of Thaumaturgy. With more than a
handful of paths and the ability to whip up an appropriate ritual, Thaumaturgy
can have so many uses.

I think someone said earlier about how Thaumaturgy doesn't have any political
use -- but it does. Whether indirectly (gathering information to blackmail) or
maybe manipulating (like Path of Corruption) it can be quite useful. And don't
forget one of the most INFAMOUS Tremere rituals -- Pavis of Foul Presence
(something like that). It makes the user IMMUNE to Presence and if someone does
try to use Presence on the user, there's a chance that the effect bounces back
(so they Entrance or Awe themselves or something). Incredibly useful in social
situations, though quite easily abused!

Halcyan 2

Messages.Author: Halcyan 2
Messages.Body:
>> It depends on how civilised the clientele are. But Neptune's Might lets you
>> see through bodies of water. Lure of Flames... yes, I suppose. But the main
>> thing about Thaumaturgy is not the paths, it's the rituals. I'm sure I

Just for fun, let's go through an analysis comparing the THA cards to the RPG
thaumaturgy. For those not familiar with the RPG, this can serve as an
education opportunity. I'm a bit rusty so please forgive any mistakes:

(For the sake of time, I won't try to explain the difference b/w Paths and
Rituals. If you're confused about it, just ask.)

Blood Rage: This is actually the second level of the Path of Blood. (One of the
few Paths that actually contains multiple cards, instead of one card simply
representing the entire path). In the RPG, you can force someone to spend a
bloodpoint on whatever you want. I guess it's a mediocre translation. Decent
damage though the strength is in impervious to Fortitude (which fits with RPG)
and the weapon-hoser part.

Blood Fury: Don't think it's actually a Path or Ritual, but probably just a
variation (improved) for Blood Rage.

Theft of Vitae: This is the 4th level of Path of Blood. Actually A LOT more
useful than in the RPG. In the RPG, you always have to worry about being
bloodbound. But it can be useful getting blood from that IV bag 10 feet away.
So Theft is a pretty good translation.

Drain Essence: Probably an improved variation of Theft.

Cauldron of Blood: Really nasty in the RPG, this is the 5th and final level of
Path of Blood. This is a very effective weapon in the RPG b/c in literally
causes blood to boil. Just about kills any mortal and can do serious damage to
vamps. In VTES, it does pretty good damage (3 or 5), though it's hamstrung by
the 2nd turn restriction.

Walk of Flame: This card represents the entire path (I think actually called
Lure of Flames). All you can really do is start fires (one of the more linear
paths), so Walk does do it some justice.

Weather Control: This also represents an entire path. In Weather Control you
start with fog and work your way up to winds, storms, and lightning. Pretty
good translation with the environmental damage. Hypothetically, it could be
useful with manuevers, presses, and damage prevention?

Movement of the Mind: My favorite path! The use in the RPG far outstrips the
VTES version. In the RPG, you can mentally lift different weight amounts. This
has so many possibilities (flying, moving people, throwing things, etc.). In
VTES, the manuever and press do a good job representing this path, but I think
some strike cards and maybe even S:CE (You fly away) good work.

Apportation: I think this is just an extension and variation for Movement of
the Mind. Great card. It's probably just a more offensive application of
Movement.

Blood to Water: This is the fifth level of Neptune's Might (a Water Path). In
RPG terms, it's sort of equivalent to Cauldron, and I think the VTES version
does it justice.

Magic of the Smith: The 2nd (?) or 3rd level of the Path of Creation. The first
level lets you make simple objects. Then one of the next two allows complex
objects (Magic of the Smith) while the other lets you destroy things you
created. This card, while not always very useful, is an excellent
representation of the many powers of the Tremere. Even if I don't use it a lot,
it should get points for just being cool!

Machine Blitz: This is a Ritual (2nd level I think). It's sort of like the Path
of Technocracy in that it messes up a machine. Decent translation. I would have
liked it better if it ALSO added a "this weapon can't be used this combat" or
something too.

Eldritch Glimmer: Another Ritual. In the RPG, you can pay blood to shoot little
green bolts at people. Really good job at converting it to VTES (with the
paying extra blood part).

Rutor's Hand: In the RPG, this was a Ritual where you cut off a hand and take
out an eye (this explains the picture, which may confuse some people). I guess
the hand/eye is just used for surveillance around your haven or something. On a
sidenote, I think there's something about not being able to regnerate your hand
while Rutor's Hand is still alive or something. I have NO idea how this
translate to the whole "get an extra untap."

Shotgun Ritual: I don't think this directly translate into a specific ritual,
but I'm pretty sure there are some rituals that speedup other magic.

Infernal Familiar: Familiars are usually owned by mages. And there IS a
background "Familiar" if you want an ex-mage who has retained his link. As for
the Infernal part. Originally in 2nd Edition, infernalism was called Dark
Thaumaturgy (separate from normal Thaumaturgy), and had it's own paths and
such. I guess Infernal Familiar fits into this category. Now adays (3rd
edition), most Dark paths are now just normal paths and Dark Thaumaturgy
doesn't really exist. There IS Daimonion(sp.) a discipline possessed by the
demon/devil-worshipping Baali... While the Sabbat does have a problem with
infernalists, and there were quite a few !Tremere who practiced it, the
!Tremere seem to always get accused of it, when a lot of them just practiced
normal Thaumaturgy!

Seeds of Corruption: In 2nd Edition, there is a Path of Corruption. You could
modify people's behavior (cause them to do the opposite thing) and even change
their personality. Don't know how this fits with the VTES version but oh
well...

Some people have theorized on how Cryptic Mission fits. In general, there is no
Path or Ritual I can remember that it is based on. On a similar note, can't
find anything for Burst of Sunlight (maybe some degree of Weather Control --
moving clouds?), and Soul Burn (maybe that Spirit Path?).

In addition, there are cards that should be Thaumaturgy ONLY:

The infamous Wake with Evening's Freshness: This is a 1st level Ritual, only
usable by those learned in thaumaturgy (obviously).

Homonculus: These are actually thaumaturgical creations (like Corpse Minions)
-- NOT Protean-related thingies.

Some of the Corruption-like cards of the Followers of Set could also be
thaumaturgy cards. While the Path of Corruption (from 2nd Edition explained
earlier) was a thaumaturgy path, FoS's could learn it w/o learning thaumaturgy.

Well, that's about all I can think of. Any additions? Suggestions? Feedback?
Hope you learned something!

Halcyan 2
